text: An explored module step can hold a selected call in flight and release it in a later step (#393, #411). life.hold(entry, *args, expected_before=None, expected_after=None, **kwargs) starts the entry and pauses its first selected call on an owned worker before target code. It reads the state once the entry, its awaitable and every other owned thread finish, so a step like Submit can expose a reservation before its worker runs. life.release(*, expected_before=None, expected_after=None) invokes no new entry: it resumes that frame and drains its worker and descendants under a fresh module deadline, so a step like Finish completes the same call. Both are module-exploration takes under all of step's checks, and sampled or non-module use fails. While a call is held, ordinary steps and declared refusals may intervene, but any second selected start fails, even when the driver catches it. A refusal leaves the hold intact, and a hold with no selected start fails unless it's a refusal declared under D-0279. A release can't declare a refusal, and an empty release is D-0200's refusal. A run that ends held drains before the next run starts, with no cleanup observations. Only hold and release rows carry an operation, the held call counts once, and Go validates operations, held status and replay on its own.
